title: The guest view is a denylist: an unpaired phone receives the learner's essay plan, and T4/M5 fields will follow
body:
## Summary
view() builds a guest's session by copying the whole Session and blanking a hand-written list of fields. Three fields added after that list was written are not on it: essayPlan (the learner's own sentences, challenge 2026-10-07), worked (M1) and workroom (T2, piece titles). A phone that has opened /phone but not joined with the code receives all three today. Every field T4 (Sittings, Spot yourself) and M5 (a failed paper's entry) adds to Session leaks the same way unless someone remembers the list.

## Description
desk/src/lib/session/pairing.ts:103-119: `const { away: _away, week, ...seen } = s;` then the guest branch returns `{ ...seen, viewer: "guest", ... }` with about 40 named resets. Session (store.ts:243-293) has about 45 top-level fields; nine were added optional later (back, watch, essayAt, essayPlan, worked, workroom, week, away, viewer). essayPlan (store.ts:260) holds the slot sentences the learner dictated on the phone (store.ts:554 essay.slot -> planFill). worked (store.ts:267) and workroom (store.ts:269, titles and counts) are also absent from the guest list. The guard test tools/desk-pairing-test.cjs:61-62 (LOBBY_EMPTY) asserts six fields, so it passes with the leak. The curtain is a settled rule (P3: the TV never lists kept texts; the shelf is phone-only), and a guest is less trusted than the TV. Smallest change: invert the guest branch to an allowlist - the guest view is built from the lobby fields it needs (screen, learner name, draft on the profile screen, phoneUrl, the pairing state) and nothing else - and make the test enumerate Object.keys of a fully populated Session and fail on any key the guest view carries that is not on the allowlist. The TV and phone branches are unchanged.

## Flow
- Today: a learner fills the Essay plan's slots on the phone; a second device opens /phone without the code; GET /api/session (route.ts:33) returns view(s, 'guest') with essayPlan.slots intact
- After: the guest receives only the lobby allowlist; a new Session field is invisible to a guest until someone adds it to the allowlist on purpose
- Test: desk-pairing-test builds a Session with every field set, asserts the guest view's keys are a subset of the allowlist and that no learner string appears in JSON.stringify(view)

## Expected impact
Closes a live privacy hole (a child's own sentences to an unpaired device on the LAN) and makes the next Session fields - T4's Sitting and Spot-yourself state (batch 6), M5's paper entry (batch 7) - private by default instead of by memory. Measured: 3 of the 9 late optional fields already missed the denylist; the guard test checks 6 of about 45 fields.

## Evaluation
Compete-now. It is a present-day data-path bug, S size, one file plus one test, and T4 (batch 6) adds Session state next. Risk is low: the guest screen is the lobby, which reads a handful of fields; the allowlist must be checked against the lobby's render (desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx guest path) so nothing the lobby needs is dropped. Because it touches the data path, the operator should confirm before it is scheduled (stop-and-ask rule).
costs: T4 (batch 6): Sitting / Spot-yourself state on Session leaks to a guest by default
M5 (batch 7): a failed paper's entry on Session leaks the same way
metric: 3 of 9 late optional Session fields missing from the guest denylist; the guard test asserts 6 of ~45 fields

title: test:rules is 63 suites in one && chain: 186 s a run, 57 copied TypeScript loaders, and the first red suite hides the rest
body:
## Summary
desk/package.json's test:rules chains 63 node processes with &&. Each process loads TypeScript (about 1.3 s) and re-transpiles what it requires (school.ts alone is about 355 ms); 57 suites carry their own copy of the loader in 9 variants. A run took 186 s wall on this base for 99.7 s inside the suites' own reported durations. The chain stops at the first failure, so a slice that moves a shared pin sees one red suite per run: M2b revised pins in 11 suites, and every batch log says the suites were green 'when run one by one'.

## Description
Measured read-only on 3fb37baf (this worktree, warm disk): `npm run test:rules` exit 0, 63 suites, 1,055 tests, 0 failed, 186 s wall; the sum of the 63 'duration_ms' lines is 99.7 s, so about 86 s is outside the test bodies (process start, `require(typescript)`, transpiling). `node -e "require('./node_modules/typescript')"` takes 1.3 s; 57 of 64 *-test.cjs files contain their own `transpileModule` hook (41 identical, 16 in 8 other spellings). Slowest suites: linga-rules 18.8 s, uat-ledger 12.1 s, maths-aim 9.6 s, maths-type 7.5 s, calc-course 5.1 s. The plan's rule 'a new suite is appended at the end of test:rules' (STUDY-DESK-V2-PLAN.md:90) is kept; only the runner changes. Smallest change: (1) tools/ts-load.cjs - the one loader (the '@/' alias, .ts and .tsx, an on-disk transpile cache keyed by the file's hash); each suite's 3-5 loader lines become one require. (2) tools/run-rules.cjs - reads the suite list from one array (or from package.json), runs every suite, prints a pass/fail table with times, and exits non-zero if any failed. test:rules becomes `node ../tools/run-rules.cjs`. Suites stay standalone (`node tools/x-test.cjs` still works).

## Flow
- Today: a builder moves a shared pin; test:rules stops at the first red suite after up to 3 minutes; they fix it, run again, hit the next one
- After: one run lists every red suite with its time; the gate's verdict is unchanged (any red suite fails it)
- The loader is shared; a transpile cache means school.ts is transpiled once per change, not once per suite that loads it (39 suites load the maths libraries)

## Expected impact
Batches 6-8 have 8 slices left, each landing 3-5 commits with the gate green at every commit (plan section f) - roughly 30-40 gate runs, plus the merge gate's own. At 186 s each that is 1.5-2 hours of wall time before the 10-23 deadline; removing most of the 86 s of per-process overhead roughly halves it, and the all-failures table removes the one-red-at-a-time loop that M2b's 11 pin revisions show. Figures to measure after: wall time of test:rules, and the sum of suite durations (unchanged by design).

## Evaluation
Compete-now, as a tools-only slice ahead of batch 6: S-M, no product code, every later slice pays it back. Risk: the runner is the merge gate, so it must keep the exit semantics exactly (any failure, a crash, or a suite that prints no result is red) - prove it with a planted red suite and a planted crash. The loader swap is mechanical but touches 57 files; do it in one commit per 10-15 suites so a diff stays readable. The suite-local root-only caveat (maths-rules 'learners case 3') is unchanged.
evidence:
desk/package.json:15  "test:rules": "node ../tools/linga-rules-test.cjs && node ../tools/maths-rules-test.cjs && ... && node ../tools/gcse-units-test.cjs"  (63 suites)
tools/school-rules-test.cjs:12-16  let ts;try{ts=require(path.join(root,'node_modules/typescript'))} ... Module._resolveFilename=... require.extensions['.ts']=(mod,file)=>mod._compile(ts.transpileModule(...)
tools/linga-rules-test.cjs:693  assert.deepEqual(callers,[...])  (the slowest suite, 18.8 s, 93 tests)
docs/concepts/STUDY-DESK-V2-PLAN.md:90  Every slice: the gate is `cd desk && npm test`, green at its commit. A new suite is appended at the end of `test:rules`.
docs/concepts/STUDY-DESK-V2-PLAN.md:295  Every suite green when run one by one
measured: 186 s wall, 99.7 s summed suite duration_ms, 1,055 tests, 57 loader copies in 9 variants, require(typescript) 1.3 s, school.ts transpile 355 ms
costs: every commit of L4, T4, T5, M3a (batch 6), M5, L5, M3b (batch 7), L6 (batch 8)
any slice that revises a shared pin (M3a, M3b, M5 grow paths)
metric: 63 suites, 186 s wall vs 99.7 s in suites; 57 copied loaders; M2b revised pins in 11 suites

title: The twin measures a sentence two ways: long-run compares the essay splitter's whitespace count with the style sheet's own sentences and words
body:
## Summary
T3's long-run detector counts words per sentence from splitSentences (essay.ts: a split needs a capital after the stop; words = whitespace tokens), then compares them with band.wps.p90 from styleSheet (style.ts: its own sentencesOf splits at every stop and every line break; words = letters and digits). On lower-case chat or line-broken messages the two disagree, and T4 (D6 plants habits inside the writer's measured bounds; D7 proves a move when the detector stops firing) and the full T5 (open habits become card constraints) both stand on that comparison.

## Description
Four sentence splitters and five word counters sit in the essay/twin/style area: splitSentences essay.ts:25-46 (words essay.ts:44 `t.split(/\s+/).length`), sentencesOf style.ts:50-52 with words style.ts:48 `[\p{L}\p{N}']+`, the playbook's split essay.ts:382, and habits' own words habits.ts:26. Concretely: 'ok see you at 6. bring the charger. thanks' is one sentence of 9 words to splitSentences (no capital after the stops) and three sentences of at most 4 words to sentencesOf - so a writer's band p90 is low and their own ordinary message reads as a long run. The T3 log already notes the English-only guard silencing terse texts; this is the other direction, a false hit, and the T3 fixture (author's own rows, mostly capitalised) would not show it. Two lesser seams T4/T5 inherit: the portrait is computed in three places with different inputs (workroom.ts:18 with exclusions, app/api/twin/route.ts:35 without, card.ts:88 with), and card.ts:110 hard-codes `constraints: []` while ChannelPortrait keeps only the dims and drops the StyleSheet that openHabits needs per channel. Smallest change: one measurement - styleSheet takes its sentences from splitSentences (or habits counts with style's words over the same sentences) - plus a fixture row of lower-case chat in habits-fixtures; keep the StyleSheet on ChannelPortrait.

## Flow
- Today: a chat writer's band says p90 = 6 words (sentencesOf); their message splits as one 14-word 'sentence' under splitSentences; long-run fires on a habit they do not have
- T4 plants that habit in a Sitting draft and asks them to prove they fixed it; T5 exports it as a 'don't' constraint on their card
- After: one splitter and one word count feed both sides; a lower-case chat row in the fixture pins it

## Expected impact
Prevents T4's planted-habit and proven-move logic, and T5's exported constraints, from being built on a comparison between two different measurements. Measured: 4 sentence splitters, 5 word counters, 2 hedge lists that disagree (style.ts:37 14 terms, habits.ts:69 13), 3 portrait computations. A shared measurement now is one function; after T4 it is a migration across its plants, proofs and their fixtures.

## Evaluation
Compete-now, as T4's first commit rather than a separate slice: S, pure functions, the habits and style suites are its gate. Risk: changing styleSheet's sentences moves T1's dims for some writers and may move style-rules / twin-probe stub pins - revise them openly, as the plan asks. If the owner prefers T1's measures frozen, take the other arm (habits measures with style's splitter and words) - the T3 gate (zero false positives) must be re-run either way.
costs: T4 (batch 6): D6 plants within measured bounds, D7 'proven' when the detector stops firing
T5 full (batch 6): open habits become exported card constraints
metric: 4 sentence splitters, 5 word counters, 3 portrait computations, 2 disagreeing hedge lists

title: Linga has two 'adult' tests - age for scenes, mode for features - and L5's 18+ romance must pick one
body:
## Summary
Which scenes a learner may play is decided by age (audienceAllowed -> isAdult, curriculum.ts:73-76); which adult features they get is decided by mode (modeOf: pitch, Cut). So a 30-year-old who chose Family mode is still offered the 'date' scene and the tutor prompt calls them 'an adult' (conversation.ts:68), while Cut and pitches are refused. The adult plan said 'never build a second mode concept' and recorded that audienceAllowed 'is not re-expressed through' modeOf; it still is not. L5 (C4, 18+ romance and nightlife, behind the red-team) gates on this, and cambridge.ts carries a third, age-only copy.

## Description
isAdult (rules/mode.ts:38-40) is age first, then type 'other' plus a confirmation; modeOf (mode.ts:47-51) honours a stored 'family' first. audienceAllowed's adult branch uses isAdult (curriculum.ts:75); eligibleScenes uses modeOf only for pitches (curriculum.ts:89); cambridge.ts:101-103 audiencesAt re-derives audiences from age alone; the 'date' scene is special-cased by id twice (curriculum.ts:121, :128). L5 has about 9 edit sites in 5 files (the tutor prompt's never-flirt line conversation.ts:75, the age line :68, the plan system prompt check.ts:158 and its rubric :165, the date exclusions, gate.ts word lists, audienceAllowed, the Cut prompt conversation.ts:129). The red-team's kill row - 'any minor reaching an adult scene' (V2 plan g) - is only testable against one definition. Smallest change: one exported `adultContent(p, prefs)` in rules/mode.ts that every audience decision calls (audienceAllowed's adult branch, the tutor's age line, audiencesAt for school-type profiles), with a mode-rules table row per profile shape; the 'date' id checks become an audience or tag on the scene. Whether Family mode hides adult scenes from an 18+ is an owner decision (it changes a Family behaviour - plan section f says stop and ask).

## Flow
- Today: profile age 30, mode family -> modeOf = family (no pitch, no Cut) but audienceAllowed('adult') = true (the date scene is offered) and the prompt says 'an adult'
- L5 adds romance and nightlife: with two tests, the red-team must cover both combinations or a scene ships under the looser one
- After: one adultContent() decides every audience; the red-team runs against it; mode-rules pins the table

## Expected impact
Makes L5's safety gate one function the red-team can be pointed at, instead of two predicates plus an age-only copy. Measured: 2 adult predicates used across 11 call sites (isAdult at curriculum.ts:75, conversation.ts:68, :75, check.ts via audienceAllowed; modeOf at conversation.ts:173, :215, curriculum.ts:89, view.ts:240, :533, turn.ts:67, :93), 1 age-only re-implementation (cambridge.ts:101), 2 id-special-cases for 'date'.

## Evaluation
Later (before L5, batch 7), but ask the owner now: the code change is S, the decision is the cost, and it should not be made inside L5's red-team. L4 (batch 6) does not need it. Risk: moving the scene gate to mode changes what an 18+ Family profile is offered (the date scene disappears) - a Family behaviour change, so owner-gated.
evidence:
desk/src/lib/english/curriculum.ts:75  return audience === "adult" ? isAdult(p, prefs) : ...
desk/src/lib/english/curriculum.ts:89  ...(modeOf(p, prefs) === "adult" ? pitchScenes(l) : [])
desk/src/lib/rules/mode.ts:38-40  isAdult: age >= 18, else type 'other' and (mode adult or adultConfirmed)
desk/src/lib/rules/mode.ts:47-51  modeOf: a stored 'family' wins
desk/src/lib/english/conversation.ts:68  The learner is ${isAdult(p,prefs)?"an adult":...}
desk/src/lib/english/cambridge.ts:101-103  audiencesAt(age): age >= 18 ? ["all", "older", "adult"] : ...
desk/src/lib/english/curriculum.ts:121, :128  the 'date' scene excluded by id
docs/concepts/ADULT-MODE-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md:165  `audienceAllowed` is not re-expressed through it
costs: L5 (batch 7): 18+ romance and nightlife gate and its red-team
metric: 2 adult predicates over 11 call sites, 1 age-only copy, 2 'date' id special cases, ~9 L5 edit sites in 5 files

title: A third math path is hard-coded out: 'calc1' at 8 sites decides judging and loading, and path lengths are pinned as literals in 10+ suites
body:
## Summary
M3b (the Calculus 2 spine) adds a path, and M3a/M5 grow existing ones. Today the path list is closed in code: kindOfTopic judges an item as Calculus only when its path is the string 'calc1' (kinds.ts:62), so a 'calc2' item would be judged 'linear'; pathChecked drops any other mathPath on load (store.ts:44); COURSES lists two (profileRows.ts:63); hint routing tests 'calc1' twice. Separately, the suites pin path lengths as literals: M2b's 15 -> 17 revised pins in 11 test files (21 files in 667102a3), and the Calculus path's 22 is pinned in 10 suites.

## Description
PATHS (lib/library/paths.ts) is a record with `school: boolean` - the right seam - but callers test the id instead: paths.ts:16 `type MathPath = "school" | "calc1"`, paths.ts:64 `profile?.mathPath === "calc1" ? "calc1" : "school"`, kinds.ts:62, store.ts:44, hint.ts:65 and :83, app/api/hint/route.ts:51, profileRows.ts:63. Pins: `grep` finds 17 literal school-length pins in 10 suites (maths-course, maths-paths, maths-ruler, maths-rules, maths-tv, school-ruler, tv-keys, voice-rules, week-rules, gcse-units) and 34 lines pinning 22 in 10 suites. M2b's log lists each revision (plan lines 449-460). Smallest change: (a) give each PATHS entry a `judge: "school" | "calc" | "linear"` (or `kind`) and replace the 8 id tests with lookups; pathChecked becomes `p.mathPath in PATHS`; COURSES = Object.keys(PATHS). (b) suites derive lengths from `PATHS[x].topics.length`, keeping one explicit length pin per path in maths-paths-test (the place a reviewer looks); ruler geometry rows compute from N.

## Flow
- M3b: add PATHS.calc2 -> today its items are judged 'linear', a stored calc2 learner loads as school, the profile row cannot offer it; after: one record entry
- M3a/M5 grow a path by k topics -> today ~10 suites fail one at a time on literal pins; after: one pin in maths-paths-test moves

## Expected impact
Turns M3b's path from an 8-site hunt (one of which silently mis-judges every item) into a record entry, and turns the next path growth from M2b's 11-suite pin revision into one. Measured: 8 'calc1' id tests in 6 source files; 17 + 34 literal path-length pins across 10 + 10 suites; M2b touched 21 files to add two topics to the path.

## Evaluation
Later: as the first commit of M3a (batch 6) for the pins, and of M3b (batch 7) for the path record - S each, and neither earns its keep before a path actually changes. Risk: the pins exist so a path change is seen; keep one explicit pin per path so growth stays a deliberate, reviewed edit.
compete: later (first commit of M3a, then M3b)
costs: M3b (batch 7): a calc2 path is judged 'linear' and dropped on load
M5 (batch 7): any new school unit on the path repeats M2b's 11-suite revision
metric: 8 'calc1' id tests in 6 files; 17 + 34 literal path-length pins in 10 + 10 suites; 21 files touched to add 2 topics

title: school.ts is 3,413 lines and a unit is 13 edit regions across it: give the next GCSE units their own module, leave the fifteen alone
body:
## Summary
lib/rules/school.ts holds the reader, the expression parser, 14 spec shapes, the question writer, slips, the checker, the leak profile, 16 generators, the task reader, unitOf, withheld and workedAnswer in one file. Adding the probability unit (M2b U2) touched about 13 separate regions between lines 366 and 3346 (175 lines added in 510759b6), Pythagoras about 12 (158 lines). M5 (recovery from a failed paper) reads these units and the coverage is 23 of 86 statements, so more units follow; the file has had 23 commits since September and 39 suites load it.

## Description
The per-shape dispatch is spread across structure (636), readKind (780), read (948), question (1081), SCHOOL_SLIPS (1200), slipCandidates (1306), check (1665), leakProfile (1963), the generators (2259-2800), GCSE_GENERATORS/SCHOOL_GENERATORS (2801, 2813), SCHOOL_UNIT_SLIPS (2838), the task reader (2868-3282), unitOf (3301), SCHOOL_WITHHELD (3332) and workedAnswer (3389). 'probability' appears at lines 366-369, 386-389, 558-560, 589, 699, 916, 1132-1142, 1262-1264, 1396, 1997, 2723-2810, 2853, 3227-3243, 3315, 3346. The M2b sweep (tools/gcse-units-test.cjs) is the right per-unit gate and already exists. A full split now would risk the fifteen existing units' verdicts (school-rules is a zero-false-right table) days before the deadline. Smallest change: a `SchoolUnit` contract (shape, structure-read, question, slips, check, leak profile, generator, task reader, worked answer) and a registry that school.ts's switches consult first; new units are written as one module each under lib/rules/school/units/; move pythagoras and probability first, proved by the gcse-units sweep and the school-* suites unchanged; the older shapes stay where they are until a slice has reason to touch them.

## Flow
- Today: a builder adding a GCSE unit for M5 edits ~13 places in a 3,413-line file that two other slices may also touch
- After: a new unit is one module plus one registry line; the sweep runs over the registry; the fifteen original units' code does not move

## Expected impact
Lowers the cost and conflict surface of every GCSE unit M5 or later work adds (each is today ~160-175 lines spread over ~13 regions of one file) and gives the sweep a registry to iterate. Measured: 3,413 lines, 63 top-level exports, 14 shapes, ~13 regions per unit, 23 commits since 2026-09-01, 39 of 64 suites load the maths libraries.

## Evaluation
Later (batch 7, as M5's first commit, or when the next unit is added). Batch 6 does not touch school.ts (L4, T4, T5, M3a are elsewhere), so competing now buys nothing before 10-23 and risks verdicts; a refactor that moves the fifteen units is not recommended before the deadline at all.
costs: M5 (batch 7): reads the units and is likely to add GCSE units (23 of 86 statements touched)
metric: 3,413 lines; ~13 edit regions per unit; 23 commits since 2026-09-01; 39 suites load the maths libraries
